html:
World War I was the war of 1914 to 1918 between the Allies, led by France, Britain and Russia and later joined by Italy and the United States, and the Central Powers: Germany, Austria-Hungary, the Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria. Around nine million soldiers died, and millions of civilians.

It began after a Bosnian Serb shot the Austrian heir, Archduke Franz Ferdinand, in Sarajevo in June 1914. Alliances pulled the great powers in within weeks. In the west the armies dug trenches from the Channel to Switzerland and fought for four years with machine guns, artillery and gas. In the east the fronts moved more, and the strain broke Russia: the Russian Revolution took it out of the war in 1918.

Empires made it a world war:

  • Soldiers and labourers came from India, Africa, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
  • Allied troops took Germany's colonies: Togoland in 1914, German South West Africa in 1915 and Kamerun in 1916. In German East Africa the Germans fought on until after the armistice.
  • At home, factories drew in women, and in the US the Great Migration brought Black workers north. A munitions ship blew up in the Halifax explosion of 1917.

The armistice came on 11 November 1918. Four empires fell, the Treaty of Versailles punished Germany, and the League of Nations handed the German and Ottoman lands to the winners as mandates. Twenty years later came the second war; see the world wars.
